description: The name now says exactly what the fixture pins: `tell`/`ask`/`each` are reserved WITHOUT the Sprites profile. All three `define`s raise `ol-reserved-word` under `core-language` alone, because `spec/grammar.md:408` makes profile words built-in names unconditionally -- what a profile decides is whether a name WORKS, never whether a program may declare it -- and issue #855 aligned `spec/turtles-and-sprites.md:154` with that ruling. HISTORY: issue #679 (SP7) wrote this as the OFF half of a profile gate, expecting all three to check clean until a program opted into Sprites; ruling #833 retracted the gate and issue #841 removed it from the checker, so the expectation is flipped here rather than the fixture deleted -- the behaviour stays pinned across the reversal, and the reversal stays visible in one file's history. `"check": true`: it asserts the checker diagnostics, not execution -- the procedures are never called and no events are produced. `message` is deliberately absent from the diagnostics below, and the asymmetry with the twin is intentional rather than an oversight: the harness does not compare `message` even when a fixture supplies it (measured -- a deliberately wrong `message` here still passed the suite), so including it would add an assertion nothing verifies. Diagnostic identity is `code` plus `params` and "prose is presentation" (`spec/error-model.md:253`); the learner-facing wording is pinned by unit tests instead. Dropping the decorative `message` from the twins is a corpus-wide edit and belongs to issue #842.
